## 

![](images/clipboard-2133479479.png){width=100}

**Goal** Does owning a smartphone influences sleep, depression, obesity?

## What we know - Linear Regression

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1x_1 + \beta_2x_2+\dots+\epsilon, \qquad \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)
$$

- The [response]{.underline} is continuous (hours of sleep)

- The [predictors]{.underline} can be continuous of categorical (age, phone ownership, etc)

- The effects of the predictos act on the mean of the response.

. . .

**Example**

> If age uncreases by one year, keeping all other predictors constant, the mean slept hours decreases by $\beta$

## Group Discussion{.smaller}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}

Our response is the answer to: 

> Does the child sleep less than 9 hours per night? Yes/No


Our predictor: 

> hours of smartphone use per day.

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggeasy)

set.seed(123)

n <- 300

hours <- runif(n, 0, 10)

eta <- -4 + 0.8 * hours
p <- plogis(eta)

df <- data.frame(
  hours,
  y = rbinom(n, 1, p))

df %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(hours, y)) + xlab(" hours of smartphone use per day") +
  ylab("Sleep less than 9hours")
```
:::



::::






**Discuss** 

- What should a good model predict?

- Can we use linear regression? 

- Do you see any possible problem/challenge with linear regression? 



## The model{.smaller}

- We want the model to predict probabilities!

- We want a linear predictor of the form $\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \dots$ 

. . .

Let's try to fit a linear regression: $y =\beta_0 + \beta_1x +\epsilon$ 
```{r}
lm_fit  <- lm(y ~ hours, data = df)

glm_fit <- glm(
  y ~ hours,
  family = binomial,
  data = df
)

grid <- data.frame(
  hours = seq(0, 10, length.out = 200)
)

grid$lm_pred  <- predict(lm_fit, grid)


ggplot(df, aes(hours, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(hours, lm_pred,
        colour = "Linear regression"),
    linewidth = 1.2
  )  +  labs(
    y = "Probability of depression",
    colour = ""
  ) + xlab(" hours of smartphone use per day") + easy_remove_legend()
```
 



## Logistic Regression

We want to find a function of the probability to link to the linear predictor such that the predicted values always  make sense!

. . .


```{r}

lm_fit  <- lm(y ~ hours, data = df)

glm_fit <- glm(
  y ~ hours,
  family = binomial,
  data = df
)

grid <- data.frame(
  hours = seq(0, 10, length.out = 200)
)

grid$lm_pred  <- predict(lm_fit, grid)
grid$glm_pred <- predict(glm_fit, grid,
                         type = "response")

ggplot(df, aes(hours, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(hours, lm_pred,
        colour = "Linear regression"),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(hours, glm_pred,
        colour = "Logistic regression"),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Linear regression" = "red",
      "Logistic regression" = "blue"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Probability of depression",
    colour = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
